svg.title: Projection versus Q-Former
svg.desc: Left, projection: each encoder frame passes through a linear layer or small MLP and becomes one LLM token, so the token count grows with the length of the audio; LLark uses 10 tokens per second and Qwen2-Audio about 25. Right, Q-Former: a small Transformer with a few learned query vectors. The queries attend to each other and cross-attend to the encoder frames, and only the query outputs go to the LLM, so each window gives a fixed number of tokens; BLIP-2 uses 32 queries per image and SALMONN one query per 0.33-second window, 88 tokens for 30 seconds.
svg.text: same linear layer or MLP per frame
Fixed tokens per window: BLIP-2 32 per image,
